scope: Effective ISO 32000-2:2020 EC3 §12.5.6.6 Free text annotations, .7 Line annotations, .8 Square and circle annotations, .9 Polygon and polyline annotations, .11 Caret annotations, .12 Rubber stamp annotations, and .13 Ink annotations. Popup and note-window behavior, text markup, annotation border/blend mechanics, and common AP mechanics are out of scope except where needed to distinguish a supplied AP from a missing-AP construction path.

The markup subclauses are reader-facing display descriptions; a no-AP constructed appearance test is not a valid producer-conformance witness for these nondegenerate annotations.

features.feature: FreeText is always visible; variable text, quadding, callout and inner text rectangle
features.source_requirements: §12.5.6.6 says the text shall always be visible (no open/closed popup state) and directs the reader to §12.7.4.3. Table 177 requires /DA; /Q defaults to left (0); /RC is used to generate appearance; /CL is meaningful only for FreeTextCallout; /IT defaults FreeText and FreeTextTypeWriter draws no callout; /RD defines the inner text rectangle; /LE is meaningful only when /CL exists and decorates its (x1,y1) endpoint. If a stored AP exists, it takes precedence over DA. EC3 #524 corrects the /RD type cell from rectangle to array. These are separate decisions: supplied AP display is governed by §12.5.5; generated fallback is the project's reader policy for absent AP, which Table 166 says the producer should have supplied here.
features.implementation_and_consumers: pdf-model/src/annotation.rs::decided and stored_set_aside select supplied AP or regenerate after a changed text value. pdf-model/src/appearance.rs::construct/free_text, free_text_layout, free_text_border generate missing-AP drawing; pdf-model/src/view/markup.rs and viewer-core/src/viewer/editing.rs expose selection/editing of existing and newly added FreeText; viewer-core host input/command reaches these operations.
features.assertions: free_text_annotation_spec_audit.rs is a standalone annotation-only fixture with exact classic xref, explicit no-recovery and complete interpretation. It checks /Q default against 0 with centered/right controls and all four /RD edges via independent ink bounds; this verifies this implementation's constructed fallback. variable_text.rs::a_free_text_annotation_the_file_states_is_retyped_redrawn_and_written_back starts with an AP solid-block control against DA text, checks AP initially wins, then verifies edited text replaces the stale stream at runtime and after save/reopen. Existing callout tests cover knee-point position, endpoint /LE, /IT condition, /RD isolation and unsupported-value reporting. Missing-AP fixtures are producer-nonconforming under Table 166 and must not be cited as a normative reader requirement.
features.residuals: The current bounds/default/callout tests cover selected Table 177 behavior, not all rich-text/XFA formatting or every border combination. Stored AP's direct initial precedence is independently visible in the retyping test, but the standalone missing-AP tests are reader-policy tests.

features.feature: Line geometry, signed leader construction, end styles, caption intent and placement
features.source_requirements: Table 178 requires /L endpoints in default user space. /LL, signed side, /LLE, /LLO, /Cap, /CP, /CO, /IT, /Measure and the endpoints /LE names each have their own conditions/defaults. Table 179 names ten ending shapes but supplies no shape dimensions; shape size is therefore an implementation choice. EC3 #515 supplies the filled RClosedArrow phrase whose row is clipped in the table extraction; it is recorded in doc/errata-read.md. The popup sentence is excluded from this shard as previously reviewed.
features.implementation_and_consumers: pdf-model/src/appearance.rs::line, leader geometry and caption helpers create the missing-AP fallback; pdf-model/src/measurement.rs reads an annotation's measure. The page annotation interpreter in content/annotations.rs consumes either the selected stored appearance or this constructed stream for rendering.
features.assertions: annotations.rs::a_line_annotations_leader_lines_put_the_line_where_the_clause_says, a_leader_line_has_an_offset_before_it_and_an_extension_beyond_it, a_captioned_line_draws_its_contents_where_cp_states, a_caption_this_table_cannot_place_is_named_and_the_line_is_still_drawn, and an_annotations_own_measure_states_the_units_its_geometry_is_in assert specific geometry/pixel or API values with controls. line_ending_endpoint_spec_audit.rs has exact-xref/no-recovery endpoint and signed-leader controls. Most no-AP shape tests exercise construction policy rather than valid producer conformance; a prior audit identifies a stale introductory comment in line_ending_endpoint_spec_audit.rs referring to the displaced ADR 0192 interpretation, although the assertions follow the current table reading.
features.residuals: No full sweep of ten endpoint shapes or all combinations of LL/LLE/LLO/captions here; the standard does not fix endpoint-shape dimensions.

features.feature: Square/Circle geometry, fill, insets and cloudy border effects
features.source_requirements: §12.5.6.8 requires a rectangle or ellipse inscribed within /Rect; unequal width and height are allowed. Table 180 assigns /BS width/dash, /IC fill, /BE border effect and /RD inset differences, with explicit nonnegative and sum-less-than-dimension limits. EC3 #524 corrects /RD's type cell from rectangle to array. The accepted common-border audit is outside current scope; this row records only subtype geometry/fill/effect behavior.
features.implementation_and_consumers: pdf-model/src/appearance.rs::square_or_circle, differences and cloudy construct the fallback shape; annotation::decided selects stored AP before construction. Rendered through the page annotation interpreter.
features.assertions: annotations.rs::a_circle_is_an_ellipse_inscribed_in_its_rectangle checks ellipse versus rectangle geometry; cloudy square/circle tests check effect silhouette/cusp; interior-colour and fill tests use pixels; test for nonzero RD and empty shape cases assert selected edge/area behavior. Annotation appearance tests use a stored AP independently to test placement/compositing, but those generic AP tests do not establish a constructed Square/Circle shape.
features.residuals: Atypical rectangle aspect ratios are exercised for Circle; this shard did not audit every square-specific RD validation branch or malformed producer values. Tests omitting AP are constructed-fallback checks, not reader conformance demands.

features.feature: Polygon closed contour versus open PolyLine; /Vertices, PDF 2.0 /Path and subtype-specific /IC
features.source_requirements: §12.5.6.9 defines Polygon as closed and PolyLine as not implicitly connecting the first and last vertex. Corrected Table 181 makes /Vertices required unless /Path exists, and says /Vertices shall be ignored if Path is present (EC3 #444). /Path sequences m/l/c operands and uses current graphics-state width/dash. /IC fills all Polygon interior but for PolyLine only line endings. /LE is meaningful only for PolyLine; /BE only for Polygon. Table 181's /Path precedence is normative, unlike Ink's.
features.implementation_and_consumers: pdf-model/src/appearance.rs::polygon, path_segments and path construct. Annotation rendering uses this only where no supplied AP is selected.
features.assertions: polygon_polyline_spec_audit.rs::polygon_path_strokes_its_closing_edge_while_polyline_path_stays_open includes decoy Vertices, a valid PDF 2.0 ID, exact xref/no-recovery and geometry pixels that distinguish closed/open contours. polyline_ic_fills_closed_endings_but_not_open_endings checks /IC on open versus closed endings and a Line positive control; polyline_first_ending_is_at_first_vertex_not_second_vertex compares to equivalent Line geometry. annotations.rs adds /IC, /LE and /BE paired checks. The no-AP drawings test fallback output, not producer conformance.
features.residuals: The focused test verifies /Path replaces /Vertices and contour closure, but not all cubic operand shapes or every producer validation rule. EC3 correction #444 is effective and should be the ledger/source baseline; don't reassert old Table 181 text.

features.source_requirements: §12.5.6.11 calls Caret a visual symbol indicating text edits but does not define artwork for the caret itself. Table 183 /RD records differences from the underlying caret; /Sy /P requires a paragraph symbol to be associated with the caret, while /None is the default. Corrected #524 calls /RD an array and #608 joins the sentence so display of the paragraph symbol is explicitly 'along with the caret'.
features.implementation_and_consumers: appearance::construct reports a policy refusal for a Caret without a stored AP rather than inventing its base shape. annotation::decided selects a stored AP if provided. The viewer's public page-render route returns the display list and unsupported notes; no separate caret-specific GUI artwork consumer was found.
features.assertions: annotations.rs::a_caret_is_reported_whether_or_not_it_asks_for_a_paragraph_symbol covers absent /Sy, /P and /None plus /RD, and checks the refusal's reason. This confirms current choice but its no-AP fixture violates Table 166's AP writer rule for nondegenerate Rect, so it is not ISO reader-conformance evidence. Generic annotation stored AP path is distinct.
features.residuals: Whether to draw a caret is a documented product boundary, not an ISO-mandated refusal; no base caret artwork oracle exists in this clause. Source #608 strengthens the accompaniment reading but cannot make /P a substitute for caret artwork.

features.feature: Rubber Stamp /Name and PDF 2.0 /IT intent with supplied AP separation
features.source_requirements: Table 184 names standard icon intents and says a reader should provide predefined icons; /Name defaults to Draft. For PDF 2.0 /IT defaults to Stamp with StampSnapshot, StampImage and Stamp defined. Producer constraint: if /IT is present and not Stamp, /Name shall not be present. This is not a reader rejection mandate. Stored AP handling is still the ordinary §12.5.5 path.
features.implementation_and_consumers: appearance::construct declines to synthesize a missing stamp appearance, while annotation::decided selects supplied AP before construct. Viewer page rendering is the public visual consumer; there is no separate stamp control UI in the reviewed path.
features.assertions: annotations.rs::a_stamps_appearance_is_reported_and_the_other_two_icons_are_drawn checks no-AP Stamp refusal, against other recommended icon cases. Its fixture supplies no annotation AP and is producer-nonconforming for a nondegenerate Rect. Draft drafts/stamp_stored_appearance.rs tests the opposite case: exact xref, no recovery, public interpretation, supplied red normal AP and expected rendered pixel; it distinguishes the standard AP route from project fallback policy. Draft is uncompiled/unrun.
features.residuals: No behavioral test of /IT interactions is needed to claim the supplied AP rule; this review did not certify all AP state selection or printing. The stamp's no-AP refusal is an explicit product choice and has no cost on the project corpus per ADR 0109/1367 census claims, not a normative mandate.

features.feature: InkList disjoint strokes and PDF 2.0 Ink /Path
features.source_requirements: §12.5.6.13 requires one or more disjoint paths. Table 185 requires /InkList and gives each point sequence in default user space; connecting samples by straight lines or curves is implementation-dependent. PDF 2.0 /Path provides m/l/c operands and inherits current graphics state. EC3 #444 (physical p.510, printed p.495) corrects Table 185 to say /InkList shall be ignored if /Path is present. The current Path-first implementation is therefore the corrected normative precedence, not a local choice.
features.implementation_and_consumers: appearance.rs::ink and path draw straight segments from InkList or cubic segments from Path; current code prefers Path when both are present, as Table 185 requires after EC3 #444. Stored AP is handled before fallback by annotation::decided.
features.assertions: ink_annotation_spec_audit.rs::an_ink_list_with_three_points_joins_each_consecutive_pair asserts two independently located segments and that no chord shortcuts the corner. ink_path_six_operands_produce_a_cubic_curve_not_an_endpoint_chord checks the cubic midpoint and excludes straight chord. Both have exact xref/no-recovery/complete interpretation and PDF 2.0 ID for Path. The conflicting InkList in the Path fixture is a useful discriminator for the corrected precedence. Missing AP makes these fallback tests, not producer conformance tests.
features.residuals: The standard intentionally leaves point connection algorithm-dependent. Existing assertions establish current Path-over-InkList behavior with a conflict fixture, but this review did not establish every possible path operand or malformed-input behavior.
